region: Watkins Glen · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Lakewood Vineyards sits on the west shore of Seneca Lake just north of Watkins Glen. The Stamp family moved to Lakewood Farm in 1951 and planted grapes the next year, selling them for decades to juice processors and large wineries. As that market faded in the 1980s, they planted fine wine varieties and founded the winery in 1988, opening the doors in 1989. Three generations now run it: Chris Stamp makes the wine, his brother Dave manages the vineyards, and the family farms about 100 certified-sustainable acres.

This Pinot Gris comes from the Gigliotti family’s vineyard, a grower whose name Lakewood has put on the label for more than a decade. The 2023 release was small, 582 cases. Lakewood makes it in a fuller, riper style than the crisp, lean Pinot Grigio many people expect, closer in spirit to Alsace: the winery describes it as lush, with melon and honeysuckle on the nose and a full, fruity finish.
